software.backgroundActivity: Push approvals and some connected sign-in/backup flows require background/network-capable operation
software.description: Authenticator for one-time codes, Microsoft account approvals, and supported sign-in flows.

evidence.claim: Microsoft documents Authenticator backup and restore behavior and notes that restore is not cross-platform between Android and iOS.
Microsoft documents that restore behavior varies by account type and that some work/school or passwordless credentials require sign-in or re-registration.

software.internetRequirement: Not required for local TOTP generation; required for push approvals, backup/restore and connected sign-in flows
limitations: Microsoft-specific push approvals are not portable to standard TOTP apps
Backup and recovery behavior is platform-dependent
software.name: Microsoft Authenticator
software.networkActivity: Local TOTP can work offline; push approvals, account backup/restore and connected Microsoft sign-in flows require network access

privacyDetails.advertising: Not documented for Authenticator itself in the checked support sources
privacyDetails.analytics: Not documented in the checked Authenticator support sources
privacyDetails.collected: Data handling varies by feature. Local TOTP generation has a different data boundary from cloud backup, push approvals, and Microsoft account sign-in flows.
privacyDetails.controls: Backup and account configuration are feature-dependent; some credentials require re-registration rather than portable export.
privacyDetails.deletion: Removing an app entry does not necessarily remove an authentication method from the underlying Microsoft/work/school account.
privacyDetails.encryption: The checked support sources describe backup/restore behavior but do not establish a universal end-to-end encryption claim for every credential type.
privacyDetails.practicalImplications: A migration must distinguish standard TOTP entries from push, passwordless, work/school, and device-bound credentials. The latter may require re-registration.
privacyDetails.purpose: Generate one-time codes, approve sign-ins, support passwordless or account-bound authentication flows, and optionally back up supported credentials.
privacyDetails.recipients: Microsoft infrastructure is involved for push approvals, backup/restore, and Microsoft-connected authentication features.
privacyDetails.sale: Not documented in the checked Authenticator support sources
privacyDetails.sharing: Cloud backup and connected authentication flows transmit data to Microsoft services; local TOTP generation does not require those flows.
privacyDetails.tracking: Not documented in the checked Authenticator support sources

software.privacySummary: Microsoft publishes privacy disclosures; local code generation and connected approval or backup features have different network needs.
